transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No. Do not use that battery again, and do not put it back on charge. This is a serious safety hazard. Please remove the battery from the charger immediately (if it isn't already) and place it in a safe, non-flammable area away from flammable materials until you can dispose of it properly. Do not attempt to puncture, crush, or repair the casing yourself. Since this is a safety-critical component that has failed catastrophically, do not try to 'fix' it. Contact Shark Customer Support or an authorised retailer for a replacement unit appropriate for your IZ201UK model.
Ok, I won't use it. It's still clicked into the vacuum and is leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels, and it has a faint chemical smell. Should I move it somewhere else?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, please move it immediately. A chemical smell combined with swelling and heat means the battery is actively failing and could ignite or release toxic fumes. Tea towels are highly flammable, so do not leave it there. Move the vacuum (with the battery still attached) to a non-flammable surface like a concrete floor, garage, or outside if possible, away from curtains, paper, or anything that can burn. Do not touch the swollen part with bare hands if you suspect heat, and ensure no one is nearby while you move it. Once it is in a safe spot, do not put it back on charge and do not try to remove the battery yourself unless you are certain it is cool and you have the right tools to avoid puncturing it. The best course of action is to take the entire vacuum unit to a local household waste recycling centre (tip) or a shop that accepts battery recycling, explaining the situation so they can handle it safely. This is not a normal wear-out; it is a dangerous cell failure. There is no safe way to continue using this battery.

candidates: Battery cell failure / internal short circuit leading to thermal runaway and swelling (high)

reading.symptom: battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam

plan: They asked: "Can I still use it till a new one comes?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
